get.summary:
The audit log, newest first. Text filters are partial or prefix matches that the indexes answer (no table scan): `entityType` is a fragment of
the entity name, `entityId`, `actor` and `action` are prefixes, `search` tries an entity name fragment and an id prefix at once.

parameters.name: EntityType
parameters.description: A fragment of the entity name, case-insensitive: "doc" finds StockDocument, "product" finds Product and ProductBarcode (see `GET /api/audit/filters`).

parameters.name: Actor
parameters.description: User name starts with (case-insensitive): "staf" finds staff.

parameters.name: AfterId
parameters.description: Seek paging: return entries older than this id.

parameters.name: EntityId
parameters.description: Id of the entity starts with: a document number such as ISS-WH01-2610-0017, a user id, a SKU prefix of the bulk events.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Action starts with: "document." for every document event, "login" for sign-ins, "document.posted" for one.

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: One box for a person: matches an entity name fragment OR an entity id prefix, so a document number and "Document" both work.

post.summary: Approves a Submitted document. The body is optional, except that a document with `requiresOverride` needs `negativeStockOverrideReason` here: the approver gives the reason, not the person who posts.
Posts an Approved (or approval-free Submitted) document. There is no request body: the override reason was recorded at approval.

get.summary:
Barcode or SKU lookup for the line picker and scanning. Always 200: `found` says whether a product owns the code
(`product` is null when it does not), because a scan that matches nothing is a normal outcome, not a failed request.

post.description: Signs in and returns the access token. The refresh token is set as an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to /api/auth. DEPRECATED: only when Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default) is the refresh token also returned in the JSON body; clients must not read it.

Rotates the refresh token and returns a new access token. The refresh token is read from the HttpOnly cookie; the browser must send credentials, the header X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest, and an Origin that is in Cors:Origins (otherwise 403). DEPRECATED: a refreshToken in the request body is still accepted and takes precedence; so is the refresh token in the response body only when Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default).

Revokes the refresh token (from the cookie, or DEPRECATED from the request body) and clears the cookie. Always 204 for an unknown or already revoked token. A cookie-authenticated call needs the same X-Requested-With header and allowed Origin as refresh.

ApprovalMetric.description: What an approval rule measures: the document value or its total quantity.

ApprovalTrigger.description: One reason a document needs approval: Actual reached Threshold of a rule that needs RoleRequired.

negativeStockOverrideReason.description: Required when the document `requiresOverride`: why the approver lets stock go below zero. Ignored for any other document.

AttachmentOwnerType.description: What a file is attached to. Adding an owner type means adding one owner policy in the application layer.

AuditFilterOptions.description: What the audit log filters can be offered as dropdowns: the entity names and action names an audit row can carry.

refreshToken.description: DEPRECATED. The refresh token now travels in an HttpOnly cookie; this property is null unless Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default).

AuthResult.description:
The result of a login or refresh. RefreshToken is null when the API is configured to deliver the refresh token
only in its HttpOnly cookie (Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody=false).

returnedToMe.description: Drafts I created that a reviewer sent back.

postedToday.description: Documents posted since local midnight (Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, BR-10), whoever posted them, that are still Posted: a document reversed since is not counted, so this equals the Posted list filtered to today.

approvalsWaiting.description: Submitted documents held for approval that I could act on: not mine to approve when self-approval is off, only large ones for the Owner, none large for a Supervisor, zero for roles that cannot approve.

DocumentCounts.description: The numbers behind the Home tiles and menu badges, for the signed-in user, within the warehouses they may see.

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the document was submitted (false for a Draft).

requiresOverride.description: An issue was submitted although stock is short (negative stock is allowed): the approver must give a reason when approving, which forces approval whatever the value thresholds say. A fact about the moment of submission: it stays true after approval and posting; the stored reason is in `NegativeStockOverrideReason`.

isLarge.description: The approval rule that fired needs a role above Supervisor (for example the Owner).

isReturned.description: A Draft that a reviewer sent back (`RejectionReason` holds why, `ReturnedBy*` who).

negativeStockOverrideReason.description: Why the approver let stock go below zero; set when a document that `requiresOverride` is approved, otherwise null.

totalAmount.description: Value of the document: receipts at their entered cost; an issue at its booked cost once posted, and before that at the average cost when it was last saved or submitted (see `AmountIsEstimate`). For a Submitted document this is the value the approval rules were tested against.

allowedActions.description: What the caller may do right now (edit, submit, approve, reject, cancel, post, reverse). The UI shows buttons from this list only. It already accounts for ownership (Warehouse staff and Clerk act only on their own documents), the approver the document is routed to (an Owner reviews only `isLarge` documents, a Supervisor the rest) and self-approval, so a listed action is one the API will accept.

approvalTriggers.description: While the document is Submitted or Approved and an approval rule held it back: which thresholds it reaches (value or quantity), for the approver and the "sent for approval" message. Empty otherwise, and when only a negative-stock override (`requiresOverride`) sent it to approval.

amountIsEstimate.description: True for an issue that has not posted yet: its lines carry the average cost seen when it was last saved or submitted, and posting books the real cost. Label the amount "estimated".

concurrencyToken.description: Changes whenever the document (header, status or lines) changes. Also sent as the ETag header; send it back as If-Match to refuse a stale save.

available.description: On hand in the document's warehouse right now, in base units (compare with `BaseQty`; lines of one product add up). Null once the document is Posted, Reversed or Cancelled, when the figure no longer says anything about this document.

totalAmount.description: Same meaning as on the full document: an unposted issue is valued at the average cost seen when it was last saved or submitted (`AmountIsEstimate`).

requiresApproval.description: An approval rule fired when the document was submitted. With `status=Submitted` this is the approvals inbox.

isReturned.description: A Draft that a reviewer sent back.

concurrencyToken.description: Same value as `concurrencyToken` on the full document: compare it to know whether an open document has gone stale.

amountIsEstimate.description: True for an issue that has not posted yet: `totalAmount` is an estimate at the average cost seen when it was last saved or submitted.

canAct.description:
The caller may approve or reject this document right now: it is Submitted and held for approval, routed to the caller's role
(an Owner reviews only `isLarge` documents, a Supervisor the rest, an Admin all) and, unless self-approval is on, not submitted by the caller.
This is exactly the rule behind the "waiting for approval" count. A single document's `allowedActions` additionally tests the live approval rules.

DocumentStatus.description: Figure 5 state machine. Rejection returns to Draft (reason kept on the document).

created.description: Rows that create (a preview reports what a commit would create).

updated.description: Rows that update an existing record (a preview reports what a commit would update).

ok.description: False when the row has errors and blocks the import.

status.description: New or Update for a valid row (what a commit would do with it; the same in a preview and after a commit), Error otherwise. A valid row can still carry a note in `Errors` (for example "unit not changed").

ImportRowStatus.description: What an import row does (or would do on commit): create something new, update something that exists, or nothing because it has errors.

qtyOnHand.description: Zero for a product that has never been stocked (it has no balance row). Negative when stock went below zero.

shortfall.description: Safety stock minus on hand: how many units are missing (more than the safety level when the balance is negative).

isNegative.description: On hand is below zero: show it as a warning, not just as "low".

total.description: Rows matching the filter, or int Paging.TotalNotCounted when the caller asked to skip the (expensive) count.

ProductLookupResult.description:
Answer to a barcode or SKU lookup. A code nobody owns is a normal outcome of scanning, not an error:
`Found` is false and `Product` is null (HTTP 200), so a scan miss does not look like a failed request.

ProductSort.description: Sort keys the products list accepts. Only these are allowed, so a client cannot sort on an unindexed column.

refreshToken.description: DEPRECATED. The refresh token now travels in an HttpOnly cookie; this property is null unless Auth:ReturnRefreshTokenInBody is switched on (off by default).

RefreshRequest.description: The refresh token to redeem or revoke. Optional on the wire: when absent, the API reads it from the HttpOnly cookie.

isLow.description: Below the product's safety stock (when it has one) or below zero.

isNegative.description: On hand is below zero: show a warning, not just a "Low" chip (also true when the product has no safety stock).

totalValue.description: Net value of the stock in the caller's warehouses (quantity x average cost). A negative balance lowers it, so it can be less than the sum of the positive lines.

skuCount.description: Products with stock: distinct products that have a positive quantity in at least one of the caller's warehouses (zero and negative balances are not counted).

lowCount.description: Product x warehouse pairs on the low-stock list (see `GET /api/stock/low-stock`): below safety stock, never stocked with a safety level, or negative. Equals that list's total.
